about.title: Costa Mesa Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Costa Mesa runs on work that gets done with hands, tools, and vehicles. Retail floors along Harbor Boulevard, warehouses and shops near the SR-55, restaurants, hotels, and construction sites across this Orange County city of roughly 113,000 people all carry their own risks. When a shift ends in an injury, the first question is usually simple: who covers this? In California, workers' compensation normally handles medical care and a portion of lost wages no matter who was at fault, and it is generally your only claim against your employer. If a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver played a part, however, a separate third-party claim may exist alongside comp. Costa Mesa logged 619 injury collisions in 2025, with 847 people hurt and four lives lost, and Newport Boulevard, Harbor Boulevard, and both directions of SR-55 saw the highest counts. If you were working when a crash happened, both paths deserve a look. LawProactive connects you, free, with an independent attorney who can sort them out.

items.question: I was driving for my job on SR-55 in Costa Mesa when another car hit me. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your wages regardless of fault. But the other driver is a third party, so a separate injury claim against them may also be available. Costa Mesa saw 619 injury collisions in 2025, many along SR-55 and Newport Boulevard, so this is a common overlap worth having reviewed.

items.question: I did not report my injury right away. Have I lost my rights?
items.answer: California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of a work injury, so report it in writing as soon as you can. Missing that window does not always end a claim, but it can complicate things. Any third-party claim runs on a separate two-year deadline, which is another reason not to wait.

items.question: Can my Costa Mesa employer fire me for filing a claim?
items.answer: Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing for workers' compensation is illegal in California. If you are demoted, cut from the schedule, or let go after reporting, that is a separate issue an attorney can address. Keep copies of your report and any messages from your employer.
